verses.text: At daybreak, all the chief priests and elders met and planned to have Jesus executed.
They tied Him up, led Him away, and handed Him over to Governor Pontius Pilate.
When Judas, who had betrayed Jesus, saw He was condemned, he regretted it. He brought the thirty silver coins back to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I sinned. I betrayed an innocent man.” They replied, “That’s your problem. Handle it yourself.”
Judas threw the silver into the temple sanctuary, left, and went and hanged himself.
The chief priests picked up the coins. “It’s against the law to put this blood money in the treasury.”
After discussing it, they used the money to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
That’s why the field has been called “Field of Blood” ever since.
Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet came true: “They took the thirty silver coins—the price set on him, the one some of Israel’s people valued—
and they used them to buy the potter’s field, just as the Lord directed me.”
Jesus stood before the governor. Pilate asked Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” Jesus answered, “That’s what you say.”
When the chief priests and elders accused Him, He didn’t answer.
Then Pilate asked Him, “Don’t You hear all these charges they’re making against You?”
Jesus didn’t answer a single word, and the governor was really amazed.
At the festival, the governor had a custom of releasing one prisoner the crowd chose.
At that time they had a well-known prisoner called Barabbas.
So when the crowd gathered, Pilate asked them, “Who do you want me to release: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
Pilate knew they had handed Jesus over because they were jealous.
While Pilate was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him a message: “Have nothing to do with that innocent man. Today I suffered a lot in a dream because of Him.”
But the chief priests and elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and have Jesus killed.
The governor asked them, “Which of these two should I release to you?” They shouted, “Barabbas!”
Pilate said, “Then what should I do with Jesus, the one called Christ?” They all shouted, “Crucify Him!”
The governor asked, “Why? What wrong has He done?” But they shouted even louder, “Crucify Him!”
Pilate saw he wasn’t getting anywhere and a riot was starting. So he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. “I’m innocent of this righteous man’s blood. You deal with it.”
All the people answered, “Let His blood be on us and our children!”
Then Pilate released Barabbas to them. He had Jesus whipped and handed Him over to be crucified.
The governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s headquarters and gathered the whole unit around Him.
They stripped Him and put a scarlet robe on Him.
They twisted thorn branches into a crown and set it on His head, then put a stick in His right hand. They knelt in front of Him and mocked Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
They spat on Him, took the stick, and hit Him on the head.
After they had mocked Him, they took off the robe, put His own clothes back on Him, and led Him away to crucify Him.
As they went out, they met a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry Jesus’ cross.
They came to a place called Golgotha, which means “Place of a Skull.”
There they offered Jesus sour wine mixed with gall. He tasted it but wouldn’t drink it.
After they crucified Him, they divided His clothes among themselves by casting lots.
Then they sat down and kept watch over Him there.
Above His head they posted the charge against Him: “THIS IS JESUS, THE KING OF THE JEWS.”
Two robbers were crucified with Him, one on His right and one on His left.
People passing by insulted Him and shook their heads,
saying, “You said You could destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days. Save Yourself! If You’re God’s Son, come down from the cross!”
The chief priests also mocked Him, along with the legal experts, Pharisees, and elders:
“He saved others, but He can’t save Himself. If He’s Israel’s King, let Him come down from the cross now, and we’ll believe in Him.
He trusts God, so let God rescue Him now if He wants Him. He said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”
The robbers crucified with Him also threw the same insults at Him.
From noon until three in the afternoon, darkness covered the whole land.
Around three, Jesus cried out loudly, “Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?” That means, “My God, My God, why have You abandoned Me?”
Some people standing there heard Him and said, “He’s calling Elijah.”
At once one of them ran, got a sponge, soaked it in vinegar, put it on a stick, and offered Him a drink.
The others said, “Leave Him alone. Let’s see if Elijah comes to save Him.”
Jesus cried out once more, loudly, and gave up His spirit.
Suddenly the temple curtain split in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and rocks broke apart.
Tombs opened, and many bodies of God’s holy people who had died were raised to life.
After Jesus was raised, they came out of the tombs, entered the holy city, and appeared to many people.
When the centurion and those guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and everything that had happened, they were terrified. “This really was God’s Son!” they said.
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and cared for Him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too was a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Pilate ordered that it be handed over.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in clean linen.
He placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut into the rock. Then he rolled a large stone across the tomb’s entrance and left.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting across from the tomb.
The next day, the one after Preparation Day, the chief priests and Pharisees went together to Pilate.
They said, “Sir, we remember that while that deceiver was alive, He said, ‘After three days I’ll rise again.’

So order the tomb secured until the third day. Otherwise His disciples might come at night, steal Him, and tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead!’ That last deception would be worse than the first.”
Pilate told them, “You have guards. Go make it as secure as you know how.”
So they went, secured the tomb, and sealed the stone, with the guards posted there.
